chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all), and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, and Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mu'adhi, said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani, freed slave of the Hashimites, said: Yahya ibn Isma'il al-Jariri said reading (from his notes): Al-Husayn ibn Isma'il said: 'Amr ibn Jumay' narrated to me, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, who said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all).

He said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) entered into the presence of Mu'awiyah, so he asked him: 'What possessed your father to kill the people of Basra, and then wander the streets at night wearing two undergarments?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'What drove him to that was his knowledge that what befall him would not miss him, and what missed him would not befall him.' He (Mu'awiyah) said: 'You have spoken the truth.' And when the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) intended to battle the Kharijites, it was said to him: 'Take your precautions, O Commander of the Faithful!' He (peace be upon him) composed: 'Which of my two days shall I escape from death? The day which is not decreed, or the day which is decreed? The day which is not decreed, I do not fear death; and if it is decreed, caution will not avail.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَصْرَةِ: The people of Basra (referring to the Battle of Siffin's aftermath or the Kharijites' initial rebellion context)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam Ali's (AS) poetry regarding divine decree and death when fighting the Kharijites?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* illustrates the Shia doctrine of *al-Jabr wa al-Tafwid* through Imam al-Husayn’s dialogue with Mu'awiyah, affirming that Imam Ali’s military actions were guided by certainty in divine decree. It further connects this to Imam Ali’s famous verse on death, emphasizing that predestination renders excessive caution either unnecessary or ineffective, a key theme in understanding the Imamate’s spiritual authority.
